questions.q: SKIB is related to OGNG in a certain way based on the English alphabe tical order. In the same way, CUCV is related to YQHA. To which of the following op tions is QIRK related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Move the first two letters four places back and the last two five places forward. Applying this to QIRK produces MEWP.
**Answer: MEWP**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ONL AZX MLJ YXV ?
questions.solution:
Read alternate terms separately. ONL → MLJ → KJH shifts every letter back two places, so KJH is the missing fifth term.
**Answer: KJH**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 1 13 28 46 67 ?
questions.solution:
The additions are 12, 15, 18 and 21, increasing by three. Next add 24 to 67, giving 91.
**Answer: 91**

questions.q: P is the sister of Q's brother R. S is the husband of Q and T is the son of S. How is P related to T?
questions.solution:
P and Q share the brother R, so P is Q’s sister. S is Q’s husband and T their son. P is therefore T’s maternal aunt.
**Answer: Mother's sister**

questions.q: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. OJH 20, MHF 25, KFD 35, IDB 55, GBZ 95, ?
questions.solution:
Every letter moves back two positions. Number increments double: +5, +10, +20, +40, then +80. Therefore GBZ 95 is followed by EZX 175.
**Answer: EZX 175**

questions.q: Select the option in which the triads share the same relationship as that shared by the given triads. LIFE - IFEL - FELI CALM - ALMC - LMCA
questions.solution:
Move the first letter to the end at each step. MUGS becomes UGSM and then GSMU, matching both given triads.
**Answer: MUGS - UGSM - GSMU**

questions.q: B, C, D, F and H have different marks. Only one person has scored between C and D. Only one person has scored between H and D. F has scored less than C and D. How many people have scored less than B?
questions.solution:
C and H must be two positions on either side of D. F is below C and D, so B is second from the top. Three people score less than B.
**Answer: Three**

questions.q: Seven boxes, D, E, F, R, S, T and U, are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. U is kept immediately above T. E is kept immediately above D. Only F is kept above S. Only two boxes are kept above U. E is not kept at third position from the bottom. How many boxes are kept between R and F?
questions.solution:
From top to bottom the boxes are F, S, U, T, R, E, D. There are three boxes, S, U and T, between R and F.
**Answer: Three**

questions.q: In a certain code language,‘soldier protect country’ is coded as ‘lu mh na’,‘entrepreneur prosper country’ is coded as ‘na ki tu’ and‘soldier entrepreneur vital’ is coded as ‘mh tu sy’.What is the possible code for 'country vital' in that language?
questions.solution:
Country appears in the first two statements and shares code na. Soldier shares mh, entrepreneur shares tu, leaving sy for vital. Country vital is therefore na sy.
**Answer: na sy**

questions.q: Hritik ranked 20 th from the bottom and 30 th from the top in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
Total students = rank from top + rank from bottom - 1. Therefore 30 + 20 - 1 = 49.
**Answer: 49**

questions.q: In a certain code language, ‘house fire gas’ is coded as ‘dy ph mt’, ‘pressure gas station’ is coded as ‘lp ph st’, ‘station house farm’ is coded as ‘st bq dy’. What is the code for 'gas' in that language? (Note: All the codes are two-letter coded only.)
questions.solution:
Gas is common to the first two statements, and ph is their common code. Therefore gas is coded ph.
**Answer: ph**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
VST, ZWX and NKL follow shifts -3 and then +1 between successive letters. FHD follows +2 and -4, so it is the different cluster.
**Answer: FHD**

questions.q: Kamal starts from Point A and drives 17 km towards south. He then takes a left turn, drives 13 km, turns left and drives 21 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 18 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
questions.solution:
South–north movement cancels: -17 + 21 - 4 = 0. East–west movement leaves him 5 km west of A. To return, he must go 5 km east.
**Answer: 5 km to the east**

questions.q: If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 93 D 7 B 5 C (69 A 3) C 26 = ?
questions.solution:
Replace the codes to get 93 - 7 × 5 + 69/3 + 26. Applying order of operations gives 93 - 35 + 23 + 26 = 107.
**Answer: 107**

questions.q: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 37.4, 34.6 45, 42.2
questions.solution:
In each given pair, the second number is the first minus 2.8. The matching pair is 69, 66.2.
**Answer: 69, 66.2**

questions.q: Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. (Counting to be done from left to right only.) (Left) @ 2 # 2 4 3 = % 8 * 1 8 @ $ 4 ! 6 4 3 * 8 = (Right) How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
The qualifying numbers are the first 2, the 8 between % and *, the 4 between $ and !, and the final 8 between * and =. There are four.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.solution:
The normal letter steps are +3, +6, +4. RUAF has steps +3, +6, +5, so it differs in the final step.
**Answer: RUAF**

questions.q: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. L is an immediate neighbour of both J and H. I is sitting second to the left of J. K is sitting third to the right of H. G is an immediate neighbour of both I and H. The position of how many persons will remain unchanged if all persons are arranged in English alphabetical order in clockwise direction, starting from G (including G)?
questions.solution:
Clockwise from G, the original order is G, H, L, J, K, I. Alphabetical order gives G, H, I, J, K, L. G, H, J and K retain their positions, making four.
**Answer: Four**

questions.q: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 16 – 17 – 21 – 30; 13 – 14 – 18 – 27
questions.solution:
Add successive squares 1, 4 and 9. The matching sequence is 22 → 23 → 27 → 36.
**Answer: 22 – 23 – 27 – 36**

questions.q: Which of the following letter-clusters should replace # and % so that the pattern and relationship followed between the letter-cluster pair on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of ::? # : OKR :: XTA : %
questions.solution:
Advance every letter four places, wrapping after Z. KGN becomes OKR and XTA becomes BXE.
**Answer: # = KGN, % = BXE**

questions.q: Refer to the given number, symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (Left) $ 7 @ 6 = & 5 Ω 4 > # 8 & % 9 1 * £ 3 (Right) How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a number and also immediately followed by another number?
questions.solution:
Only @ between 7 and 6, and Ω between 5 and 4, have a number on both sides. Therefore two symbols qualify.
**Answer: Two**

questions.q: If in a code language, If ‘A’ stands for ‘÷’, ‘B’ stands for ‘×’, ‘C’ stands for ‘+’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘−’, then the resultant of which of the following would be 55?
questions.solution:
Replace the symbols in the second option to get 16/112 × 63 + 77 - 31 = 9 + 77 - 31 = 55.
**Answer: 16 A 112 B 63 C 77 D 31**

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 17 22 37 62 97 ?
questions.solution:
Differences are 5, 15, 25 and 35, increasing by ten. The next difference is 45, giving 97 + 45 = 142.
**Answer: 142**
